analysis.summary: Srivari Spices and Foods Limited published its investor presentation for H1 FY26, detailing financial performance, operational metrics, and strategic expansions. Management highlighted product portfolio additions including new oil products, soya chunks, and a puja devotional articles vertical named 'Neihaa Narayan'. The company reported strong financial growth with higher revenues, EBITDA margins, and return ratios alongside expanded distribution reach across retail and modern trade. Management discussed Srivari Spices and Foods Limited's financial performance, business segments, and growth strategies during the investor conference call for FY25 and Q1 FY26. The company operates in traditional staples through Srivari and has launched a new e-commerce and grocery vertical called Poushtik, alongside a new edible oil manufacturing plant that began commercial production on 10th May 2025.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that the Indian soy protein market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 6 percent from 2024 to 2029.
demand_outlook.quote: The Indian soy protein market is projected to grow at a CAGR of ~6% from 2024 –2029, driven by rising health awareness and higher protein consumption.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that the market size for spices is over two lakh crores, with approximately 70% currently in unorganized trade.
demand_outlook.quote: As I said, one important thing is in the spices, still 70% is an unorganized trade.

capex_expansion.claim: The company launched a new oil plant and officially introduced its products in Mumbai on 28 July 2025.
capex_expansion.quote: Launched a new oil plant and officially introduced its products in Mumbai, Maharashtra on 28 July 2025 .

capex_expansion.claim: The company launched its new edible oil production plant, which started commercial production on 10th May 2025.
capex_expansion.quote: and we launched our edible oil on 10th May 2025 and it started its commercial production on 10th May 2025.

capex_expansion.claim: The installed capacity for spices and masalas is 3,600 tons per annum, atta is 14,400 tons per annum, and oil is 7,200 tons per annum.
capex_expansion.quote: For spices and masalas, we have an installed capacity of 3,600 tons per annum with the current utilization at about 2,637 tons. When it comes to atta, 14,400 tons per annum installed capacity and we have utilized 12,650 tons. Regarding oil, we have installed capacity of 7,200 tons per annum but this plant is yet to be commercialized.

margins_costs.claim: The EBITDA margin stood at 17.05% for H1 FY26.
Management noted that PAT decreased due to the new plant commencement and claiming six months of depreciation.
margins_costs.quote: See PAT has been decreased due to the new plant commencement and we have claimed the depreciation of the 6 months because of that PAT has been decreased, but our overall numbers are positive.

capital_allocation.claim: Rights shares were issued on 10th October 2024 to enhance the capital structure.
capital_allocation.quote: Rights Shares issued on 10th Oct, 2024 to enhance capital structure.

capital_allocation.claim: The entire amount raised from the rights issue was utilized for specified purposes without any deviation.
capital_allocation.quote: So, as disclosed in the letter of offer, we have utilized the entire amount for the specified purpose without any deviation.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that all oil products will be placed in complete marketplaces by the end of the month.
management_commitments.quote: All the oil product will be placed in the complete marketplaces.
